\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قرض} \fa{گرفتن} (qarz gereftan)}{قرض گرفتن (qarz gereftan)}]{\fa{قرض} \fa{گرفتن} (qarz gereftan) — to borrow}

\label{lesson:FA-C411-qarz-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a document, then the Persian for citizenship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قرض} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{قرض} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{qarz gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to borrow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{از} \fa{دوستم} \fa{کمی} \fa{پول} \fa{قرض} \fa{گرفتم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{az dustam kami pul qarz gereftam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I borrowed a little money from my friend.
\end{quote}

\emph{Qarz} \textquotedblleft{}loan\textquotedblright{} + \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} (stem \emph{gir-}). \emph{Az kasi qarz gereftan} — to borrow from someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{قرض} \fa{گرفتن}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}to take a loan\textquotedblright{}: \emph{qarz} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{qarḍ} \textquotedblleft{}a loan\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), and \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qarz gereftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{qarz gereftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a document, then the Persian for citizenship, then say \emph{qarz gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{قرض} \fa{گرفتن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To borrow\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قرض} \fa{دادن} (qarz dâdan)}{قرض دادن (qarz dâdan)}]{\fa{قرض} \fa{دادن} (qarz dâdan) — to lend}

\label{lesson:FA-C411-qarz-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for citizenship, then the Persian for to borrow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قرض} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{قرض} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{qarz dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to lend\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برادرم} \fa{ماشینش} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{من} \fa{قرض} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{barâdaram mâshinash râ be man qarz dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother lent me his car.
\end{quote}

\emph{Qarz} + \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} (stem \emph{deh-}). \emph{Be kasi qarz dâdan} — to lend to someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{قرض} \fa{دادن}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}to give a loan\textquotedblright{}: \emph{qarz} comes from Arabic \emph{qarḍ} \textquotedblleft{}a loan\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), and \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} is traced by EtymDB to PIE \emph{deh\textsubscript{3}-}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qarz dâdan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for citizenship, then the Persian for to borrow, then say \emph{qarz dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بدهی} (bedehi)}{بدهی (bedehi)}]{\fa{بدهی} (bedehi) — a debt}

\label{lesson:FA-C411-bedehi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to borrow, then the Persian for to lend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بدهی}}
\textbf{\fa{بدهی}} (\emph{bedehi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a debt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{همه} \fa{بدهیهایش} \fa{را} \fa{پرداخت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u hame-ye bedehihâyash râ pardâkht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He paid off all his debts.
\end{quote}

From \emph{bedeh} \textquotedblleft{}owing\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{بدهی}} is native Persian, built on \emph{bedeh} \textquotedblleft{}owing\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{deh-}, the present stem of \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, with the noun suffix \emph{-i}: what you still have to give.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بدهکار} (bedehkâr)}{بدهکار (bedehkâr)}]{\fa{بدهکار} (bedehkâr) — in debt, owing; a debtor}

\label{lesson:FA-C411-bedehkar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to lend, then the Persian for a debt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بدهکار}}
\textbf{\fa{بدهکار}} (\emph{bedehkâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}in debt, owing; a debtor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{من} \fa{هنوز} \fa{به} \fa{تو} \fa{بدهکارم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{man hanuz be to bedehkâram.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I still owe you.
\end{quote}

\emph{Be kasi bedehkâr budan} — to owe someone. The opposite is \emph{talabkâr}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{بدهکار}} is native Persian, built from \emph{bedeh} \textquotedblleft{}owing\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{deh-}, the present stem of \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, + the agent suffix \emph{-kâr}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{طلبکار} (talabkâr)}{طلبکار (talabkâr)}]{\fa{طلبکار} (talabkâr) — a creditor; owed money}

\label{lesson:FA-C411-talabkar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a debt, then the Persian for in debt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{طلبکار}}
\textbf{\fa{طلبکار}} (\emph{talabkâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a creditor; owed money\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{طلبکارها} \fa{هر} \fa{روز} \fa{به} \fa{او} \fa{زنگ} \fa{میزنند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{talabkârhâ har ruz be u zang mizanand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
His creditors call him every day.
\end{quote}

\emph{Talab} \textquotedblleft{}claim\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-kâr}. Of a person who acts as if everyone owes him: \emph{talabkâr ast}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{طلبکار}} joins \emph{talab} \textquotedblleft{}claim\textquotedblright{}, from Arabic \emph{ṭalab} \textquotedblleft{}seeking\textquotedblright{}, to the Persian agent suffix \emph{-kâr}: the one who has a claim.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
